title: VRS mode get in shader baker export incorrectly gets override for target platform
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible with 4.6.2 but can still be observed on current master.

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable (99f266575) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8253) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 63.13 GiB memory

### Issue description

We are working with some ports and one of them has a specific quirk where VRS mode is not supported but if you disable it, the game instantly crashes. (not exactly relevant but is a setup) This means that we had for this platform add a setting override to set VRS mode to Texture with an empty texture to circumvent the problem. 
This didn't work however and it seemed to ignore the setting override.

Looking through the engine code I ended up in `shader_baker_export_plugin.cpp` where GLOBAL_GET is used to fetch the current setting with overrides for the current platform. The issue itself is that the current platform during export is the editor (so, windows) making the export ignore the setting.

I was able to 'fix' the issue by simply replacing:
`int vrs_mode = GLOBAL_GET("rendering/vrs/mode");`
with this:
`int vrs_mode = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features("rendering/vrs/mode", p_features);`
which fixes the problem, correctly getting the override from the target export platform.


### Steps to reproduce

Create a platform override for rendering/vrs/mode using a feature different than the editor platform e.g: windows when on linux and set it to a different value. Export the game and observe via a print or similar that the non-overridden setting is used.
